claim: Cross-consistency assessment (pairwise value compatibility) shrinks a morphological field by about 90-99 percent, so a box with 10^4-10^6 configurations needs only hundreds of pair judgments.
agent_test: Run the same open problem with (i) free listing, (ii) full box without pruning, (iii) box with LLM pairwise CCA then code enumeration; equal tokens; score coverage of reference solutions and validity of survivors.

claim: The reduction figures all come from the method's developer (Ritchey); no independent project measures the reduction or the decision quality afterwards.
agent_test: Measure on our agent: fraction of configurations the LLM CCA removes versus a held-out expert/ground-truth feasibility label.

claim: CCA checks pairs only, so triple-wise conflicts are missed and judgments are opinion; independent groups gave diverging assessments.
agent_test: Seed known 3-way conflicts in a toy box; count how many survive pair-only CCA and whether a final verification pass (G) catches them.
note_d: LLM pairwise judges flip on swapped order in 7-28% (easy) and 25-44% (hard) of pairs (Sage); no morphological compatibility study found.

claim: No controlled experiment with an effect size shows that a morphological box raises idea quality over free ideation. Evidence is case reports (about 80 applications, 52 catalogued fields).
agent_test: Our own equal-token A/B: box versus free listing versus verbalized sampling, scored by blind novelty/validity raters.

claim: In human studies, morphological analysis is not clearly better than other methods: more elaborated concepts than brainstorming but not more concepts or diversity (N=102); morphology users did slightly worse than non-users on fluency and flexibility (N=244, non-significant); combination gave no between-group originality gain over control.
agent_test: Compare box vs plain brainstorming on fluency, flexibility, elaboration at equal tokens; expect elaboration gain, no breadth gain.

claim: Combination (the core of morphological analysis) helps, but classification or categorising helps as much or more; combination cost raw quantity.
agent_test: Test a category-first step (classify the space) versus combine-first on the agent.

claim: The matrix is often misused as a screening filter rather than a synthesis tool; traditional teams stop at 1-2 combinations with no stated reason.
agent_test: Require the agent to log why each option was dropped; compare to unlogged runs on final quality.

claim: Matrix software that forces an explicit reduction strategy led teams to build more combinations (3-64 versus 1-2) but develop each less; significance was not reached (8 teams).
agent_test: Vary number of combinations carried forward (1, 5, 30) at fixed tokens; measure depth versus breadth.

claim: Design spaces from student matrices are huge (6,144 to 3.6e13 configurations), so full enumeration is infeasible and a pruning rule is required.
agent_test: Count configs in our boxes; test code-side pruning (random sample, constraint pruning, rank-based trimming) against full enumeration where feasible.

claim: Morphological analysis loads prefrontal activity more than TRIZ and more than brainstorming (fNIRS, N=30); this is a process proxy, not a quality result.
agent_test: Not testable on an LLM; treat as weak human-process evidence only.

claim: Unstructured LLM idea generation saturates: of 4000 seed ideas only about 5 percent are non-duplicates (cosine 0.8), and many LLMs give near-identical outputs (similarity over 0.8 in 79 percent of cases).
agent_test: Measure unique-idea yield per token for free sampling versus attribute-box sampling.

claim: Prompt-level diversity fixes work: GPT-4 pool cosine similarity ranges 0.255-0.432 versus 0.243 for human groups; verbalized sampling gives 1.6-2.1x creative-writing diversity; personas help in parallel prompts.
agent_test: Compare box-driven sampling against verbalized sampling and persona prompting at equal tokens.

claim: Attribute-dimension prompts (a box run by code) beat plain prompts for diversity and matched accuracy at 5 percent of the query cost; random sampling of configurations was used because full enumeration was too costly.
agent_test: Port to design/reasoning tasks: LLM proposes dimensions, code samples cells, compare to plain.
note_d: Boundary: constraint satisfaction falls with many simultaneous attributes (37% at 50, small model); attribute sampling that varies a noisy dimension lowered F1 (ProgGen).

claim: Facet decomposition and facet-wise judging improve LLM ideation tools and novelty judgments (CSI median 70.5 vs 61.0, N=22; novelty classifier accuracy 0.78 vs 0.47 for unstructured prompt).
agent_test: Judge candidates facet by facet versus holistically; measure agreement with human labels.

claim: LLM judges are weak at ranking ideas (accuracy near chance, 43-56 percent), so an LLM cannot be trusted to pick the best cell without outside checks.
agent_test: Use code or tests to verify survivors; compare with LLM self-ranking at equal tokens.

claim: LLM ideators fixate on prompt details and drop promising concepts early; explicit prompting for alternatives is recommended but untested.
agent_test: Test an alternatives-forcing instruction versus none.

claim: Over-generate-and-rank LLM ideas were rated more novel than human experts' (5.64 vs 4.84, N=49 each), slightly weaker on feasibility; AI ideas also homogenise writers' outputs (+5.2 percent similarity).
agent_test: Check whether box-based generation also homogenises across runs; track cross-run similarity.

claim: Only one direct LLM-on-matrix study exists with numbers (McIntosh 2026: ChatGPT-4o ranking 4 scenario views over 10 issues; best view 88 percent); the LLM reads a box, it does not build one, and agreement is not tested.
agent_test: Build the box with the LLM, enumerate with code, run twice for reproducibility.

claim: LLM-assisted box construction papers (Chen 2024, Park and Geum 2025, Nomaguchi 2025) report gains but no numbers were retrieved; they are leads only.
agent_test: Obtain full texts before relying on them.
note_d: Gap search could not open Chen 2024 (403) or Park and Geum 2025; numbers still missing.

claim: Structured LLM pipelines of a fixed method are inconsistent across runs (AutoTRIZ: 7 of 10 textbook cases match or half-match in top 3; entropy up to 6.64 over 100 runs).
agent_test: Run the box-building step several times; measure agreement of dimensions across runs.
note_d: Taxonomy-generation studies also show run-to-run instability (0.285 of sibling pairs repeat in 324 runs).

claim: Injecting random constraints or personas into LLM idea prompts raises pairwise diversity over plain prompting (0.735 and 0.757 vs 0.679, GPT-4o); independent single-idea sessions (0.452) and serial 'bolder' refinement (0.575) lower it.
schema_part: S3 (code samples cells, avoid serial refine)
agent_test: Compare random-cell box sampling, random personas and plain sampling at equal tokens; measure pairwise embedding diversity and validity.

claim: Cross-model pooling gives human-level diversity (0.763 vs 0.773) while no single model does; volume alone closes coverage slowly (nearest-neighbour distance 0.546 to 0.478 for 10x ideas).
agent_test: Check whether varying model or persona across box cells beats single-model enumeration on cross-run similarity.

claim: LLM pairwise judges are order-unstable: intra-pair instability 0.07-0.28 on easy and 0.25-0.44 on hard sets, and humans reach 0.33 on complex tasks; rubrics cut it by 16%.
agent_test: Run each compatibility pair in both orders and with a rubric; treat disagreement as unknown and verify downstream.

claim: A code-side validity filter plus diversity cues around an LLM generator raised validity from 0.16 (random) and 0.52 (zero-shot, same model) to 0.82 and diversity score from 0.27 to 0.64 (robot-hand design, 90 designs).
agent_test: Port the LLM-proposes, code-filters-with-hard-rules pattern to our box and compare validity at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-built category structures are unstable across runs: only 0.285 of sibling pairs recur in all runs (0.391 at T=0, 0.178 at T=1) even when entity coverage is F1 0.995; a consensus core can be recovered from repeats.
agent_test: Build the box 3-5 times at low temperature, keep dimensions and values appearing in a majority, list the rest as extras.

claim: For large fields, a pairwise covering array (every value pair at least once) is a proposed pruning rule, and coverage-prior sampling is another; neither has been tested against random cell sampling for idea quality.
agent_test: Compare random, covering-array, and diversity-greedy cell selection at equal cell count on coverage of reference solutions.

claim: Zwicky's 'unconsidered configurations' is an originator's claim (via Ritchey), not an empirical result; no count of overlooked configurations has been found.
agent_test: Count in our test how many reference solutions free listing missed but the box produced.

claim: No study found for: LLM-versus-expert pair-compatibility agreement, independent measurement of cross-consistency reduction, or category-first versus combine-first for LLMs.
agent_test: Answer by our own test.
